questions.question: When one die is thrown once, how many possible outcomes are there in all?
questions.explanation: There are 6 outcomes, from 1 to 6.

questions.question: When one 100-yen coin and one 10-yen coin are tossed at the same time, how many possible ways can they land heads or tails in all?
questions.explanation: Each coin can land heads or tails, 2 ways each, so 2×2=4 ways (heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads, tails-tails).

questions.question: When a large die and a small die are thrown at the same time, how many possible outcomes are there in all?
questions.explanation: For each of the 6 outcomes of the large die, the small die has 6 outcomes. 6×6=36 ways.

questions.question: When the three people A, B, and C line up in a row, how many different arrangements are there in all?
questions.explanation: 3 choices for the first position × 2 for the second × 1 for the third = 6 ways.

questions.question: When two of the three cards 1, 2, and 3 are arranged to form a two-digit integer, how many integers can be made in all?
questions.explanation: 3 choices for the tens place × 2 for the ones place = 6 integers (12, 13, 21, 23, 31, 32).

questions.question: When 2 teams are chosen from the 4 teams A, B, C, and D, how many ways are there to choose in all (order does not matter)?
questions.explanation: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD — 6 ways. In a combination, order is not distinguished.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the meaning of "equally likely"?
choices: Every outcome can be expected to occur to the same degree
The same outcome happens over and over
The outcome turns out as predicted
questions.answer: Every outcome can be expected to occur to the same degree
questions.explanation: It means that, like each face of a fairly made die, every case can be expected to occur to the same degree.

questions.question: When all possible cases number n and are equally likely, and event A occurs in a of those cases, which expression represents the probability that A occurs?
questions.explanation: Probability = (number of cases in which the event occurs) ÷ (total number of cases) = {{a}}/{{n}}.

questions.question: When one die is thrown, find the probability of rolling a 3.
questions.explanation: Out of 6 outcomes in all, rolling a 3 is 1 outcome. The probability is {{1}}/{{6}}.

questions.question: When one die is thrown, find the probability of rolling an even number.
questions.explanation: Even numbers are 2, 4, and 6 — 3 outcomes. {{3}}/{{6}}={{1}}/{{2}}.

questions.question: When one die is thrown, find the probability of rolling a 5 or higher.
questions.explanation: 5 or higher is 5 and 6 — 2 outcomes. {{2}}/{{6}}={{1}}/{{3}}.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the value of a probability?
questions.explanation: The probability of an event that never occurs is 0, and the probability of an event that always occurs is 1, so a probability p satisfies 0≦p≦1.

questions.question: When two coins are tossed at the same time, find the probability that both come up heads.
questions.explanation: There are 4 outcomes (heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads, tails-tails), and both heads is 1 outcome. {{1}}/{{4}}.

questions.question: When two coins are tossed at the same time, find the probability that one comes up heads and one comes up tails.
questions.explanation: Heads-tails and tails-heads — 2 outcomes. {{2}}/{{4}}={{1}}/{{2}}.

questions.question: When three coins are tossed at the same time, find the probability that all three come up tails.
questions.explanation: There are 2×2×2=8 outcomes, and all three tails is 1 outcome. {{1}}/{{8}}.

questions.question: When a large die and a small die are thrown at the same time, find the probability that the sum of the numbers rolled is 7.
When a large die and a small die are thrown at the same time, find the probability that both show the same number.
questions.explanation: Doubles are the 6 cases (1,1) through (6,6). {{6}}/{{36}}={{1}}/{{6}}.

questions.question: When a large die and a small die are thrown at the same time, find the probability that the sum of the numbers rolled is 4 or less.
questions.explanation: The sum is 2 in 1 case, 3 in 2 cases, and 4 in 3 cases, for 6 cases in total. {{6}}/{{36}}={{1}}/{{6}}.

questions.question: When one ball is drawn from a bag containing 3 red balls and 2 white balls, find the probability of drawing a red ball.
questions.explanation: Out of 5 balls in all, 3 are red. {{3}}/{{5}}.

questions.question: When one ball is drawn from a bag containing 2 red balls, 3 white balls, and 5 blue balls, find the probability of drawing a white ball.
questions.explanation: Out of 10 balls in all, 3 are white. {{3}}/{{10}}.

questions.question: When one ticket is drawn from a lottery of 5 tickets that includes 2 winning tickets, find the probability of winning.
questions.explanation: Out of 5 tickets, 2 are winners. {{2}}/{{5}}.

questions.question: When the probability that event A occurs is p, which expression represents the probability that A does not occur?
questions.explanation: (Probability that A does not occur) = 1 - (probability that A occurs) = 1-p.

questions.question: When one die is thrown, find the probability of not rolling a 1.
questions.explanation: The probability of rolling a 1 is {{1}}/{{6}}. The probability of not rolling a 1 is 1-{{1}}/{{6}}={{5}}/{{6}}.

questions.question: When two coins are tossed at the same time, find the probability that at least one comes up heads.
questions.explanation: The opposite of "at least one heads" is "both tails", which has probability {{1}}/{{4}}. 1-{{1}}/{{4}}={{3}}/{{4}}.
